definitions.explanation: A person who has gone before and paved the way in a particular field, serving as a model or guide for those who follow.

examples.japanese: {先達|せんだつ}の{教|おし}えに{学|まな}ぶ。
examples.english: To learn from the teachings of predecessors.

examples.japanese: この{分野|ぶんや}の{先達|せんだつ}たちの{努力|どりょく}があってこそ{今|いま}がある。
examples.english: It is thanks to the efforts of pioneers in this field that we are where we are today.

examples.japanese: {先達|せんだつ}が{残|のこ}した{業績|ぎょうせき}を{引|ひ}き{継|つ}ぎ、さらに{発展|はってん}させていくことが{私|わたし}たちの{使命|しめい}だ。
examples.english: Our mission is to build on the achievements our predecessors left behind and develop them further.

notes:
Composed of {先|せん} (ahead, before) + {達|だつ} (reach, attain). A respectful term for those who came before in a field or endeavor. Has a somewhat literary or formal tone.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {先達|せんだつ}に{倣|なら}う (follow the example of predecessors)
- {先達|せんだつ}の{知恵|ちえ} (wisdom of predecessors)
- {先達|せんだつ}の{教|おし}え (teachings of predecessors)
- {先達|せんだつ}として (as a pioneer/guide)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {先駆者|せんくしゃ} — pioneer, trailblazer (more emphasis on being the first)
- {先輩|せんぱい} — senior (in school or workplace, closer social relationship)
- {前任者|ぜんにんしゃ} — predecessor (specifically in a position or role)

CULTURAL NOTE:
The famous opening of {徒然草|つれづれぐさ} (Essays in Idleness) uses the phrase {先達|せんだつ}はあらまほしきことなり — "It is desirable to have a guide." This classical usage gave the word a lasting literary association.
